messages:
maria: Nightly perf alert: generation.p99 jumped ~28% at ~2026-03-19T02:00Z. Alert: https://redwood.internal/dash/nightly-gen

deploy-bot: Rolling deploy finished: release/main @ commit 4b7c1d9 (v1.24.1) — rollout complete in us-east-1 at 01:58Z

kevin: I saw the alert. CI microbench for that commit looked fine, but those don't exercise long-running KV cache patterns. Can someone pull a flamegraph from the 02:10 job?

olga: quick findings from 02:12 profile:
- kernel selection: notable shift to "fallback_matmul" for many attention blocks
- batching: median batch size dropped from 11 -> 6 after deploy
- kernel launch latency increased on small batch paths
- KV cache: hit-rate for prefix 'sess:' decreased 0.9 -> 0.66

sam: interesting — fallback_matmul is used when we force lower workspace allocation. Was there a config change in that release? I remember PR #3010 mentioned workspace thresholds.

maria: PR 3010 adjusted kernel memory thresholds and introduced dynamic-workspace-scaling. It was meant to reduce OOMs. CI passed but maybe the thresholds are too conservative and push kernel selector to slower code paths.

kevin: I checked the merge and there's also a change in batching heuristics: "aggressive-flush-on-noisy-queue" enabled by default. That will flush partially filled batches to improve p50, but could collapse avg batch size and kill throughput.

olga: telemetry shows many 1-3 sized batches for models with long contexts; token throughput per GPU dropped ~18% at 02:00.

ci-bot: Perf CI flagged a small regression in microbench (1.05x slower) but within tolerance. No blocking failure.

maria: plan suggestion: 1) temporarily disable aggressive-flush flag to see batch size recover 2) raise workspace threshold to avoid fallback_matmul 3) add compatibility code for KV key formats (we saw mixed encodings around 02:00)

sam: I'll run a quick canary with aggressive-flush=off on a small fleet at 03:30Z. If p99/backpressure improves we'll roll the toggle cluster-wide.

kevin: I'll also run a targeted bisect between commits 4a..4b to pinpoint the kernel threshold change. If bisect points at workspace threshold, we need a tuned policy: don't force fallback_matmul unless memory pressure high AND avg batch < 4.

olga: adding a note: KV key change was in PR #3002 where we switched to 64-bit key prefix for perf. Logs show ~0.7% keys still using old 128-bit prefix, causing misses. I'll push a normalization shim to accept both formats for 48h.

maria: recording rollout-blocker and linking ticket PERF-4784. Owners: @sam, @kevin. If canary at 03:30 shows >15% p99 reduction we proceed with toggle. Also add temporary perf alert for batch-size median drop.

perfbot: Nightly alert acknowledged. Created PERF-4784. Next update expected after canary at ~03:50Z. :hourglass:
